description: What this shows: Consensus proposals and validations received from peers, and transaction relay efficiency for this node.  —  Use it to: Check that peers are feeding this node proposals, validations, and transactions, and gauge relay overhead.

panels.title: Peer Proposal Receive Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many consensus proposals this node receives from peers per second.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of received proposals over 5 minutes, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A steady rate roughly proportional to the number of proposing validators.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; scales with validator count and connectivity.*

###### Watch for:
*A drop toward zero (isolation from the network) or a sudden flood far above baseline (proposal spam).*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus** *(network event)* — the protocol by which validators agree on the next ledger's transaction set and close time.
- **Proposal** *(network event)* — a validator's advertised set of candidate transactions for the next ledger, revised each round.
- **Proposers** *(network event)* — the count of validators whose proposals this node heard in the last closed round.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::onMessage(TMProposeSet)`

###### References:
[Consensus](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/consensus-structure) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#consensus)

targets.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(sum by (service_instance_id, xrpl_branch, xrpl_node_role, xrpl_work_item) (rate(span_calls_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role", span_name="peer.proposal.receive"}[$__rate_interval])), "series", "Proposals Received / Sec", "", ""), "xrpl_ident", ", ", "service_instance_id", "xrpl_branch", "xrpl_work_item"), "xrpl_ident", "[$1]", "xrpl_ident", "(?:, )*(.*[^, ])(?:, )*")

panels.title: Proposals Trusted vs Untrusted
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The share of received proposals that come from trusted (UNL) validators versus everyone else.*

###### How it's computed:
*Received-proposal rate split by trust status over 5 minutes, shown as proportions.*

###### Reading it:
*A healthy node with a good UNL shows a solid trusted slice.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; a meaningful trusted fraction is expected.*

###### Watch for:
*A collapsing trusted share or a large untrusted volume, consistent with proposal flooding from non-UNL peers.*

###### Keywords:
- **Proposal** *(network event)* — a validator's advertised set of candidate transactions for the next ledger, revised each round.
- **Trusted / untrusted / duplicate** *(per node)* — message classification: trusted (from UNL validators), untrusted (others), or duplicate (already seen).
- **UNL (Unique Node List)** *(per node)* — the list of validators a node trusts not to collude; the basis for its consensus and quorum.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::onMessage(TMProposeSet)`

panels.title: Reduce-Relay Peer Selection
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How transaction relay picks peers: chosen relay sources, suppressed peers, and peers with the feature off.*

###### How it's computed:
*Current peer counts in each category (selected, suppressed, not-enabled), per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A high suppressed-to-selected ratio means relay is saving bandwidth as intended.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; suppressed should exceed selected in a well-connected mesh.*

###### Watch for:
*A large not-enabled count (older peers forcing full relay) or selected climbing while suppressed falls.*

###### Keywords:
- **Reduce-relay** *(per node)* — an optimization that relays messages through selected peers only, suppressing redundant forwarding.
- **Transaction suppression** *(per node)* — dropping a transaction already seen from another peer, so it is not reprocessed.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[MetricsRegistry.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/MetricsRegistry.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerReduceRelayGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#reduce-relay)

panels.title: Reduce-Relay Missing-Tx Frequency
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often a peer has to fetch a transaction it missed because relay suppressed it.*

###### How it's computed:
*The reported frequency of on-demand missing-transaction fetches, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; near-flat means suppression is well tuned.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; a low, stable value is expected.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising trend, meaning suppression is too aggressive and the on-demand fetch path is growing.*

###### Keywords:
- **Reduce-relay** *(per node)* — an optimization that relays messages through selected peers only, suppressing redundant forwarding.
- **Transaction suppression** *(per node)* — dropping a transaction already seen from another peer, so it is not reprocessed.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*
